result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both use similar dark slate themes with well-separated date, title and body in the incidents. B sets the uptime figures in a monospace face, so they line up as a true column, and its incident body text is a lighter gray that reads more easily than A's dimmer gray. A right-aligns the percentages but uses proportional figures, and the trailing 'uptime' labels make 100% sit unevenly against the other rows. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both pages are clean dark designs with a clear hierarchy of uppercase labels, titles and metadata, and neither scrolls sideways. A sets the uptime figures in a monospace font, so they are guaranteed to line up as a column, and its incident text is brighter and easier to read. B's incident body text is a dimmer gray, its percentages use the proportional font, and its main text looks slightly smaller, although B's green status banner is the nicer summary.
